html:
Borobudur, the largest Buddhist monument in the world, was built in central Java in the late 700s and early 800s under the Sailendra dynasty of Mataram. It was probably finished around 825.

It is a stepped pyramid of grey volcanic stone built over a hill, with nine platforms, six square and three round, topped by a dome. Pilgrims walk around it, climbing level by level, past 2,672 carved relief panels that tell the life of the Buddha and Mahayana stories, up to 72 perforated stupas, each holding a seated Buddha. The climb was meant to mirror the path from desire to enlightenment.

Soon after, the rival Sanjaya line built the Hindu Prambanan temples nearby. Power in Java moved east in the 900s, possibly after eruptions of Mount Merapi, and Borobudur was abandoned under ash and jungle. The British governor Stamford Raffles had it cleared in 1814. It was restored in the early 1900s and again with UNESCO's help in the 1970s and 1980s. It is comparable in ambition to Angkor Wat.
sum: Borobudur, the largest Buddhist monument in the world, was built in central Java in the late 700s and early 800s under the Sailendra dynasty of Mataram. It was probably finished around 825.
